header.stance: 油價下跌、標售需求強，長天期美債跟上漲勢

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 油價跌破$80，長天期美債跟上漲勢

週二油價再跌，20年期公債標售也獲強勁認購，帶動美債漲勢延伸至長端。10及30年期殖利率各下跌4個基點，分別收在4.43%與4.93%，表現優於前端。前一天，長債收盤持平，短中期券也回吐了大部分早盤漲幅。

美伊協議接近簽署，荷姆茲海峽通行可望恢復，布蘭特原油因此下跌5.06%至$78.96。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點至2.29%，貢獻了名目殖利率跌幅的大部分。住宅開工大減，也讓投資人在Kevin Warsh首場Fed決策前，更有理由買進長天期債券。

不過，整體通膨並沒有油價看起來那麼樂觀。5月進口物價漲幅接近預期的2倍，非燃料項目也明顯上漲，市場仍反映約75%的年底前升息機率。日本將利率升至1%，澳洲雖暫停升息，卻未排除再升。信用市場也有分化：輝達新債交易活絡，但價格沒有明顯上漲；弱勢借款人則面臨稅務爭議、付款展延與私募信貸違約增加。政府債殖利率下降，並未帶動風險資產普漲，科技股反而重挫。

## 進口物價偏熱、住宅開工大減，Fed決策前訊號分歧

2及5年期美債殖利率各下跌2個基點，分別至4.05%與4.16%。長端漲幅較大，使2年與10年期、2年與30年期利差各收窄2個基點，來到38及88個基點。10年期相對表現也較強，2s10s30s蝶式利差下降2個基點至−12個基點；5年期落後兩側天期，2s5s10s則上升2個基點至−16個基點。

2、5、10及30年期殖利率一週分別下降8、10、10及8個基點，一個月則下降4、10、16及19個基點。週二的牛市趨平延續了長端在月度區間的相對強勢，也扭轉週一漲勢主要集中在中期券的情況。

10年期名目殖利率下降，主要來自通膨補償收斂。其實質殖利率僅下跌1個基點至2.14%，損益兩平通膨率則下跌3個基點。5年期實質殖利率反而上升2個基點至1.80%，7年期持平於1.96%，20及30年期各下降2個基點至2.50%與2.70%。投資人降低了長端通膨溢價，但在對政策較敏感的天期，並沒有做出同等幅度的寬鬆預期調整。

5月進口物價正是市場仍有戒心的原因之一。月增1.9%，高於預期1.0%，年增6.7%；其中燃料月增12.5%，非燃料也月增0.8%、年增3.7%。出口物價則月增1.3%、年增11.2%。即使原油持續回落，漲價範圍如此廣泛，也意味商品供應鏈中已累積的價格壓力不會立即消失。

住宅市場則顯露高融資成本的影響。開工月減15.4%，降至年率118萬戶，為2020年以來最低。多戶住宅大減40.2%，占了大部分跌幅，單戶住宅也減少1.9%至88.2萬戶；建照核發下降0.7%至141萬戶。開工統計的信賴區間較寬，多戶住宅本來就容易波動，因此不能單憑這次降幅認定整體經濟已出現轉折，但高房貸成本與待售庫存確實正在壓抑住宅建築。

交換市場幾乎確定6月17日會維持利率不變。當時一項市場定價仍反映約75%的年底前升息機率，直到1月才完整計入1碼升幅；相較週一落在2027年3月，時間有所提前，也顯示預期尚未穩定。眼前暫停調整的確定性，遠高於下一步的方向。

SOFR選擇權交易同樣反映這種分歧。前一週成交量最高較平常多50%，部位涵蓋延後升息、今年升息1次以上，以及把降息推遲至2027年等不同情境；週二也有交易押注7月會議周邊的額外風險溢價。整體持倉不重、略偏看空債券，若Warsh展現耐心，前端仍有明顯上漲空間；但長債選擇權偏斜顯示，投資人對防範債券下跌的需求高於防範上漲。

新主席會不會改變Fed的溝通方式，也是焦點。Warsh曾批評政策指引過多、官員發言過於頻繁，使投資人開始思考季度經濟預測摘要與點陣圖是否會縮減。目前並未決定減少公布；但即使政策立場沒有更鷹派，指引變少也可能放大單次數據公布對市場的影響。

## 20年期標售需求強，長天期買盤獲得支撐

$130億20年期公債續發，得標殖利率4.927%，投標倍數2.75，高於5月較大規模、$160億新券發行時的2.55。間接投標人獲配71.57%，直接投標人獲配19.94%，交易商僅承接8.48%。這筆票息5.000%的債券於6月22日交割、2046年5月到期。參與情況良好，但缺少同時點的發行前交易報價，無法比較得標殖利率是否優於或遜於標售前水準。

短券標售則好壞參半。財政部發行$650.01億6週國庫券，最高得標利率3.600%，與前次相同。投標倍數由3.25降至3.12，但間接投標人獲配從58.67%升至69.06%；直接投標人與交易商分別獲配2.17%及28.76%。這批國庫券6月18日發行交割。次級市場短券殖利率大致平穩，沒有明顯的即時資金緊俏跡象。

標售認購踴躍，不代表債券已全部落入長期持有人手中。加拿大、德國及義大利的債務管理官員表示，避險基金有助改善流動性與價格發現。在加拿大，避險基金占標售需求的30%至50%，有時會先持有債券、再於次級市場分銷，扮演類似交易商的角色。義大利債務主管則警告，這些部位在市場不穩時可能成為系統性風險。新增買盤有其價值，但承受壓力的能力，仍取決於槓桿、融資條件與最終投資人結構。

## 股權連結融資暢通，困境信用的壓力逐漸浮現

意法半導體（STMicroelectronics）股價已接近年初的3倍，公司趁勢推介$15億可轉換債券，分別於2031及2033年到期。其中$7.5億將用於償還2027年到期的零息債，其餘作一般用途。2031年期券次的票息區間為0%至0.5%，轉換溢價47.5%至52.5%；2033年期票息0.625%至1.125%，轉換溢價50%至55%。

公司先前已將資料中心營收預測倍增至$10億。股價強勢使低票息再融資成為可能，不過推介期間股價仍跌約3%。債券持有人可參與未來股價上漲，較高轉換溢價則延後可能出現的股權稀釋；上述條件仍屬詢價範圍，尚非完成發行的定價。

輝達新債則開始接受次級市場檢驗。7年期券成交量達$12億，但整筆$250億交易的價格仍接近發行價，最長3個券次的利差在接近午間時小幅走寬。這是今年美國第二大高評級發債，最高訂單達$850億，投資人撤單不多。活絡交易顯示流動性充足，卻沒有立即帶來新券溢價。

Man Group提醒，累積的AI債券供給可能是更大的考驗。其引用摩根士丹利估計，AI與大型雲端業者的投資級發債可能達$4,000億，高收益另有$650億，合計接近總發行量的20%；相較之下，網路與科技業在2001年的發債高峰為$850億。風險較高的是自由現金流仍為負的新興雲端與資料中心業者：在AI投資回報尚未確立前，就透過高收益債或槓桿貸款擴張。

戰略產業則取得另一種資金支持。Phoenix Tailings獲得美國國防部附條件的$5億長期貸款承諾，用於興建目標2028年完成的稀土加工廠；6月稍早也獲能源部$6,600萬。貸款撥付前仍須完成財務、法律與技術審查。政府支持改善了長期資金取得，但工廠仍須完成建設並投入營運。

對困境企業而言，融資安排愈來愈圍繞著回收價值的保全。Optimum Communications警告，債權人若強制執行擔保權並進行債轉股，可能使負債$260億的集團產生逾$40億稅負。爭議核心是借款超過$200億的CSC Holdings。貸款人質疑分拆出合併報稅集團所產生稅負的規模，也質疑這項威脅本身，因此不能將其直接視為確定扣減回收價值的負債。

私募信貸的壓力也愈來愈明顯。Kroll Bond Rating Agency借款人指數的違約率升至約3年歷史以來最高。高借款成本、承作標準爭議，以及容易受到AI衝擊的軟體業曝險，預期也將增加這個$1.8兆產業的贖回需求。指數反映借款人狀況惡化，但單靠這項數據，還不能認定已發生系統性流動性危機。

Brightline從債權人取得的是更多時間，尚非最終重整方案。其12%通勤鐵路債券持有人，將未付利息的寬限期延至月底，並豁免一項涉及5月$2,220萬借款的違約。提供該筆營運資金的是Assured Guaranty，該公司也承保逾$10億優先順位債券。展延將銜接7月1日$22億優先順位債及$11億公司債的付息日，Brightline總負債則約$55億。

股市下跌之際，信用ETF表現溫和：LQD上漲0.12%，HYG下跌0.01%，JNK下跌0.02%。相較這些小幅波動，個別融資與困境債務協商更能呈現借款人之間的差異。

## 日本升息至1%，歐洲仍憂能源漲價的後續影響

日本央行以7票對1票將基準利率調高25個基點至1%，創1995年以來最高，Toichiro Asada投下反對票。央行表示，是否繼續升息將取決於經濟與通膨。油價上漲已迅速反映在企業交易價格，央行也警告，消費物價與長期預期若進一步走高，可能使基礎通膨超過目標。

10及20年期日本公債殖利率各上升7個基點。日圓在決議前短暫升值，之後交易於每$1約¥160.35；隔夜交換反映約54%的10月前再升息機率。即使這次升息早已充分預告，匯率偏弱仍是疑慮。

日本央行也為購債縮減提供較明確的終點。從2027年4月起，每月購債將維持約¥2兆，不再主動繼續調降；但隨既有債券到期，持債規模仍會縮小。這讓債券投資人更容易預估央行買盤，卻不代表回到量化寬鬆時期的支持程度。

韓國央行公布的5月會議紀錄顯示，多位委員思考的是何時升息，而非是否升息。當次決議以分歧票數維持2.5%，一位反對者主張立即升息25個基點，避免通膨預期根深蒂固。6個月利率預測指向上行，半導體活動與油價走強，也使成長及通膨預測調高。家庭槓桿、韓元偏弱與金融穩定風險，進一步增加決策壓力。

澳洲央行在3次升息開始影響經濟活動後，維持4.35%不變，但仍認為通膨過高，保留再次升息的可能。決議符合市場預期，卻沒有為寬鬆循環背書。

歐元區勞動數據稍有改善。第1季每小時勞動成本年增3.2%，較前期修正後的3.4%放緩，也低於預估3.3%。工資與薪資增加3.4%，高於非工資成本；營建業勞動成本增加4.1%。職缺率由上季2.2%微升至2.3%，但仍低於一年前。

ECB官員仍強調能源衝擊尚未完全傳導。首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，4個月的高能源價格，已為食品、商品與服務帶來延續至明年的影響。Gabriel Makhlouf及Jose Luis Escriva也提醒，即使荷姆茲協議達成，供應鏈與能源流動也不會立刻恢復正常。投資人仍預期至少再升息25個基點。

財政消息則讓歐洲各國債券面臨不同考驗。英國財政大臣Rachel Reeves向債券投資人表示，希望2029年平衡預算、降低對債市的依賴；英國公債殖利率已是七大工業國最高。這項目標超出現行財政規則，尚不是已完成的整頓方案。法國央行則將2026年成長預測降至0.5%，低於政府假設的1%，通膨預估由1.7%升至2.5%，並估計若無進一步節制，赤字將達GDP的5.2%。

中國數據呈現製造業成長與內需疲弱並存。零售銷售年減0.6%，前5個月固定資產投資下降4.1%，民間投資下降7.1%；工業生產仍年增4.5%，由出口導向與高科技活動帶動。市場期待更多政策支持，但消費與投資前景偏弱，不只影響中國資產，也牽動商品出口國。

## 菲律賓完成全年海外商業借款計畫

菲律賓透過3個美元券次籌得$25億，其中包含$3億續發，規模由原訂$20億擴大。訂單達最終發行量的4.4倍；新10年期定價美債加92.5個基點，低於初步約125個基點，5.5年期則由85收斂至55個基點。這筆交易完成2026年預定的海外商業借款，免除了今年剩餘的發行執行需求，但預算赤字仍將帶來長期融資需要。

印尼企業面對的本地市場較不穩定。政策干預、匯率創低與政府債殖利率波動之後，最高評級印尼盾公司債的30天年化波動率升至23%，為2022年以來最高。今年發行量仍增加11%，達76.8兆印尼盾，創同期紀錄。匯率弱勢使海外融資吸引力下降，企業更加依賴本地債市，卻可能必須縮小單筆規模或提高票息，才能取得足夠需求。

中國在香港發行人民幣150億元主權債，包含人民幣45億元2年期，票息1.29%創新低，整體認購倍數3.86。但債券需求強勁的同時，資金也變貴：在季底與監理需求已壓縮銀行資金之際，1個月離岸人民幣借款成本升至2個月高點。發債增加了離岸主權市場的規模，也動用了企業共用的人民幣流動性。

玻利維亞國內封鎖開始緩解，一位財政官員提及匯率統一與潛在IMF協議，帶動2031年到期美元債上漲2.3美分至100.8。兩項政策都尚未落實，價格反映的是正常化前景改善，而非融資安排已經完成。

智利在紐約時間17:00之後公布決議，一致通過維持4.5%，已連續4次會議不變。央行表示，經濟活動轉弱，使通膨風險較為平衡，但中東不確定性與石油供應問題仍未解決。週一經濟學家預期未來降息、交換市場卻反映較高利率的落差，也未因這次維持不變而消失；何時恢復降息，仍無定論。

整體基金表現不如菲律賓發債熱絡。儘管美債殖利率與美元下降，EMB仍小跌0.04%。智利披索及波蘭茲羅提受惠於布蘭特回落，但各市場的融資條件依舊差異明顯。

## 接下來看能源供應恢復與Fed決策

WTI下跌5.82%至$76.05，布蘭特下跌5.06%至$78.96。油價一週跌逾13%，一個月約跌28%。接近定稿的美伊協議增加了新的供應細節，包括允許伊朗立即出售石油、日後動用遭凍結資產，以及至少$3,000億開發融資。這些仍是擬議條件，並非已完成的石油銷售或資金撥付。

實際產能恢復需要更久。QatarEnergy預期，荷姆茲海峽恢復安全通行1個月後，LNG產出可回到約50%產能。即使協議如期6月19日簽署，航道重新開放與生產恢復仍是不同步驟；當天美國固定收益市場休市，累積消息將留待下一個交易日反映。

股市則回吐部分週一漲幅。S&P 500下跌0.57%，Nasdaq 100下跌1.89%，半導體指數下跌5.71%，跌勢集中在先前大漲的科技股。VIX上升1.30%至16.41，仍較一週前低17.4%；美元指數下降0.09%至99.54，黃金大致持平，上漲0.07%至$4,330.90。雖然能源變便宜有利美債，其他市場對風險承擔的支持，已不如週一一致。

眼前焦點是6月17日美東時間08:30的零售銷售、14:00的FOMC決議與14:30的Warsh記者會。市場預期維持3.50%至3.75%。零售控制組、經濟預測與是否偏向升息，將影響前端能否跟上能源通膨補償下降帶來的行情。

海外方面，英國6月17日公布消費者物價，18日由英國央行決策，目前政策利率為3.75%。瑞典、瑞士及挪威央行也在這兩天公布決議，印尼與菲律賓央行則面對匯率及輸入性通膨壓力。表決分歧與政策說明，將顯示油價下降究竟增加了多少觀望空間。

6月18日美東時間11:30標售$700億4週與$750億8週國庫券，13:00續發$240億、票息1.250%的5年期TIPS。週二售出的6週國庫券也在當天交割。6月19日全天休市前，值得留意Fed決策後的TIPS需求，以及集中交割期間的資金狀況。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Long Treasuries Join the Rally as Oil Drops Below $80

The Treasury rally reached the long end on Tuesday as oil fell again and a well-supported 20-year auction helped bonds hold their gains. Ten- and 30-year yields each declined 4 basis points, to 4.43% and 4.93%, outpacing the front end. A day earlier, the long bond had finished unchanged while shorter maturities surrendered much of an early rally.

Brent dropped 5.06% to $78.96 as the US-Iran agreement moved closer to a signing and raised expectations for renewed traffic through Hormuz. Ten-year inflation compensation fell 3 basis points to 2.29%, accounting for most of the nominal yield decline. Housing starts also slumped, giving investors another reason to buy duration ahead of Kevin Warsh's first Fed decision.

The inflation picture was less reassuring than oil alone suggested. May import prices rose almost twice as fast as expected, with substantial increases outside fuel, and markets still assigned roughly 75% odds to a hike before year-end. Japan raised rates to 1%, while Australia paused without ruling out another increase. Credit investors were selective too: Nvidia's new bonds traded actively but showed little price appreciation, and distressed borrowers faced tax disputes, payment extensions and rising private-credit defaults. Lower government yields did not produce a broad rally in risk assets; technology shares fell sharply.

## Hot Import Prices Meet a Housing Slump Before the Fed

The 2- and 5-year Treasury yields each fell 2 basis points, to 4.05% and 4.16%. With longer maturities gaining more, 2s10s and 2s30s each narrowed 2 basis points, to 38 and 88. The 10-year also outperformed on a relative basis: 2s10s30s fell 2 basis points to -12, while 2s5s10s rose 2 to -16 as the 5-year lagged its wings.

Over a week, 2-, 5-, 10- and 30-year yields were down 8, 10, 10 and 8 basis points; over a month, the declines were 4, 10, 16 and 19. Tuesday's flattening thus extended the long end's monthly outperformance, reversing Monday's narrower, belly-led advance.

The fall in inflation compensation was especially important at 10 years. Its real yield declined just 1 basis point to 2.14%, against the 3-basis-point breakeven drop. Five-year real yields rose 2 basis points to 1.80%, and the 7-year was unchanged at 1.96%; 20- and 30-year real yields each fell 2 basis points, to 2.50% and 2.70%. Investors were removing more inflation premium at the long end without making an equally dovish adjustment nearer the policy-sensitive part of the curve.

May import prices explained some of that caution. They rose 1.9% from April, versus a 1.0% consensus, and 6.7% from a year earlier. Fuel imports jumped 12.5% on the month, but nonfuel prices also increased 0.8% monthly and 3.7% annually. Export prices rose 1.3% and 11.2%, respectively. Even if cheaper crude persists, the breadth of the increase leaves price pressure already working through traded goods.

Housing showed the strain of expensive financing. Starts fell 15.4% to a 1.18 million annualized pace, the weakest since 2020. Multifamily construction plunged 40.2%, accounting for most of the decline, while single-family starts fell 1.9% to 882,000. Permits eased 0.7% to 1.41 million. A wide confidence interval and the volatility of multifamily building argue against reading the headline as an economy-wide turning point, but high mortgage costs and unsold inventory were clearly weighing on residential construction.

Swaps treated a June 17 hold as nearly certain. One contemporaneous measure still put the probability of a hike before year-end near 75%, with a full quarter-point increase not priced until January. That was earlier than Monday's March 2027 pricing, underscoring how unsettled the outlook remained. A pause was much more certain than the direction of the next move.

SOFR options trading reflected that uncertainty. Volumes had run as much as 50% above normal during the previous week, with positions spanning delayed hikes, one or more increases this year and cuts deferred into 2027. Tuesday's flows also targeted more premium around the July meeting. Light positioning with a modest bearish bias left scope for a front-end rally if Warsh sounded patient, while long-bond option skew showed stronger demand for protection against a selloff than against a rally.

Investors were also considering whether the new chair would change how the Fed communicates. Warsh has criticized the amount of policy guidance and the frequency of officials' public comments, raising questions about the future of the quarterly Summary of Economic Projections and dot plot. No reduction had been decided. Less guidance could leave individual data releases carrying more weight, even without a more hawkish policy stance.

## A Strong 20-Year Auction Highlights Demand for Duration

The $13 billion 20-year reopening stopped at 4.927%, drawing bids equal to 2.75 times the amount offered, versus 2.55 at May's larger $16 billion new issue. Indirect bidders took 71.57% and direct bidders 19.94%, leaving dealers just 8.48%. The 5.000% coupon bond settles June 22 and matures in May 2046. Participation was strong, although the absence of a contemporaneous when-issued quote prevents a tail-or-through comparison.

The shorter auction was more mixed. Treasury sold $65.001 billion of 6-week bills at a 3.600% high rate, unchanged from the prior sale. Cover slipped to 3.12 from 3.25, but indirect awards rose to 69.06% from 58.67%. Direct bidders took 2.17% and dealers 28.76%; the bills issue and settle June 18. Secondary bill yields were broadly steady, offering little sign of an immediate funding squeeze.

Strong auction participation does not necessarily mean bonds have reached permanent holders. Debt managers from Canada, Germany and Italy said hedge funds were improving liquidity and price discovery. In Canada, funds account for 30%-50% of auction demand and sometimes warehouse bonds before distributing them in the secondary market, acting much like dealers. Italy's debt chief warned that those positions could become a systemic risk during instability. The added buying capacity is useful, but its resilience depends on leverage and financing as well as the eventual investor base.

## Equity-Linked Funding Opens Up as Distressed Credit Strains Grow

STMicroelectronics used a share price almost three times its level at the start of the year to market $1.5 billion of convertible bonds due in 2031 and 2033. It earmarked $750 million to redeem zero-coupon notes due in 2027, with the balance for general purposes. The 2031 tranche was offered at a 0%-0.5% coupon and a 47.5%-52.5% conversion premium; the 2033 carried a 0.625%-1.125% coupon range and a 50%-55% premium.

The chipmaker had doubled its data-center revenue forecast to $1 billion. Its equity rally made low-coupon refinancing possible, though the shares fell about 3% during marketing. Bondholders receive participation in future equity gains, and the high conversion premiums delay potential dilution; the financing was still being marketed rather than completed at those indicative terms.

Nvidia's newly issued debt offered a different test after Monday's large order book. Trading in the 7-year note reached $1.2 billion, while prices across the $25 billion deal stayed close to issue levels and spreads on the three longest maturities widened modestly by late morning. The offering had been the year's second-largest US high-grade transaction, with peak orders of $85 billion and little investor attrition. Active trading showed liquidity, but not an immediate premium for owning the new bonds.

Man Group warned that cumulative AI supply could be much more demanding. Citing Morgan Stanley estimates, it said AI and hyperscaler borrowing could reach $400 billion of investment-grade bonds and another $65 billion of high yield, together approaching 20% of total issuance. Internet and technology issuance peaked at $85 billion in 2001. The concern was greatest for cash-flow-negative neocloud and data-center borrowers financing investment through high-yield bonds or leveraged loans before returns were established.

Strategic industry found another source of capital. Phoenix Tailings received a conditional $500 million long-term loan commitment from the Pentagon for a rare-earth processing plant targeted for 2028, following $66 million from the Energy Department earlier in June. Financial, legal and technical reviews must be completed before the loan closes. Government backing improves access to patient funding, but the plant still has to be built and operated.

At the distressed end of the market, financing was increasingly about preserving recoveries. Optimum Communications warned that creditor foreclosure and a debt-for-equity exchange could trigger more than $4 billion of tax liabilities across a group with $26 billion of debt. The dispute centers on CSC Holdings, which has more than $20 billion of borrowings. Lenders questioned both the size of the potential deconsolidation tax bill and the threat itself; neither should be treated as a settled claim on recoveries.

Private-credit stress was also becoming more visible. Defaults in Kroll Bond Rating Agency's borrower index reached the highest level in its roughly three-year history. High borrowing costs, disputed underwriting standards and software exposure vulnerable to AI were expected to add to redemption requests in the $1.8 trillion industry. The index showed worsening borrower outcomes, though not by itself a system-wide liquidity break.

Brightline gained more time from creditors rather than a final restructuring. Holders of its 12% commuter-rail bonds extended a missed-payment grace period through month-end and waived a default linked to a $22.2 million borrowing in May. Assured Guaranty, which insures more than $1 billion of senior bonds, supplied that working-capital loan. The extension runs into July 1 coupons on $2.2 billion of senior debt and $1.1 billion of corporate notes, against total debt of about $5.5 billion.

Listed credit funds were subdued alongside the decline in equities. LQD rose 0.12%, while HYG slipped 0.01% and JNK fell 0.02%. The financing transactions and distressed negotiations offered a more differentiated picture than those small fund moves alone.

## Japan Raises Rates to 1%; Europe Still Sees Energy Aftershocks

The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark 25 basis points to 1%, the highest since 1995, in a 7-1 vote with Toichiro Asada dissenting. It said further increases would depend on the economy and inflation. Higher oil costs had already passed quickly through business transactions, and the bank warned that broader consumer prices and long-term expectations could push underlying inflation above target.

Ten- and 20-year JGB yields each rose 7 basis points. The yen traded near 160.35 per dollar after briefly strengthening before the decision, and overnight swaps put the chance of another increase by October at about 54%. The weak currency remained a concern despite a well-telegraphed hike.

The BOJ also provided a firmer endpoint for reductions in bond buying. From April 2027, it plans to hold monthly purchases near ¥2 trillion rather than continue actively reducing them. Its portfolio will still shrink as securities mature. The decision offers greater predictability for bond buyers without returning to the scale of support seen during quantitative easing.

Minutes released from the Bank of Korea's May meeting showed several members viewing tightening as a question of when rather than whether. The bank had held at 2.5% in a split decision, with one dissenter favoring an immediate 25-basis-point increase to prevent expectations from becoming entrenched. Six-month rate projections pointed higher, and growth and inflation forecasts were raised as semiconductor activity and oil costs strengthened. Household leverage, a weak won and financial-stability risks added to the concerns.

Australia held at 4.35% after three increases began to weigh on activity. The RBA still described inflation as too high and retained the option of another rise. The pause delivered the expected decision without endorsing an easing cycle.

Euro-area labor data were somewhat more reassuring. Hourly labor costs rose 3.2% from a year earlier in the first quarter, slowing from a revised 3.4% and coming in below the 3.3% estimate. Wages and salaries increased 3.4%, faster than non-wage costs, while construction labor costs rose 4.1%. The vacancy rate edged up to 2.3% from 2.2% over the quarter, but remained below a year earlier.

ECB officials nevertheless emphasized the lagged energy shock. Chief Economist Philip Lane said four months of high energy prices had set up wider effects on food, goods and services into next year. Gabriel Makhlouf and Jose Luis Escriva also cautioned that supply chains and energy flows would not return to normal immediately after a Hormuz agreement. Investors continued to expect at least another 25-basis-point increase.

Fiscal news gave investors additional reasons to distinguish among European borrowers. UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves told bond investors she aimed to balance the budget in 2029 and reduce reliance on debt markets, with gilt yields already the highest in the Group of Seven. That ambition went beyond current fiscal rules; it was not yet a completed consolidation plan. In France, the central bank cut its 2026 growth forecast to 0.5%, compared with the government's 1% assumption, raised its inflation forecast to 2.5% from 1.7%, and projected a deficit of 5.2% of GDP without further restraint.

China's data highlighted weak domestic demand beneath manufacturing growth. Retail sales fell 0.6% from a year earlier, fixed-asset investment contracted 4.1% in the first five months, and private investment dropped 7.1%. Industrial production still grew 4.5%, led by export-oriented and high-technology activity. Expectations of more policy support sat alongside a weak consumption and investment outlook, with implications for commodity exporters as well as Chinese assets.

## The Philippines Completes Its Overseas Borrowing Plan

The Philippines raised $2.5 billion in three dollar tranches, including a $300 million reopening, after enlarging the sale from $2 billion. Orders reached 4.4 times the final size. A new 10-year priced at 92.5 basis points over Treasuries, versus initial talk near 125; the 5.5-year tightened to 55 from 85. The sale completed planned external commercial borrowing for 2026, removing that year's remaining execution requirement even as the budget deficit sustains longer-term funding needs.

Indonesia's corporate borrowers faced a more unsettled local market. Thirty-day annualized volatility in top-rated rupiah bonds reached 23%, the highest since 2022, following policy intervention, a record-low currency and volatile government yields. Issuance was still up 11% this year at 76.8 trillion rupiah, a record pace for the period. Companies increasingly depend on local bonds as currency weakness makes overseas funding less attractive, but may need smaller deals or higher coupons to secure demand.

China sold 15 billion yuan of sovereign bonds in Hong Kong, including 4.5 billion of 2-year notes at a record-low 1.29% coupon. The sale was 3.86 times subscribed. Demand for the bonds coincided with more expensive cash: one-month offshore yuan borrowing costs reached a two-month high as quarter-end and regulatory needs were already pressing banks. The issuance adds to the offshore sovereign market while drawing on the same yuan liquidity pool used by companies.

Bolivia's 2031 dollar bonds rose 2.3 cents to 100.8 as domestic blockades began to ease and a Treasury official pointed to foreign-exchange unification and a possible IMF agreement. The market move preceded delivery of either policy. It reflected improving prospects for normalization rather than a completed financing arrangement.

Chile unanimously held at 4.5% for a fourth meeting in a decision announced after 17:00 New York time. The central bank said inflation risks had become more balanced as activity weakened, while warning that Middle East uncertainty and oil supply remained unresolved. The decision follows Monday's gap between economists expecting eventual cuts and swaps implying a higher rate path; it did not settle when easing might resume.

Broad fund performance was less buoyant than the Philippine sale. EMB slipped 0.04% despite lower US yields and a softer dollar. The Chilean peso and Polish zloty benefited from falling Brent, but borrowing conditions continued to differ sharply across markets.

## Oil Supply Recovery and the Fed Decision Come Next

WTI fell 5.82% to $76.05 and Brent dropped 5.06% to $78.96. Oil was down more than 13% over a week and about 28% over a month. New details of the near-final US-Iran agreement contemplated immediate Iranian oil sales, eventual access to frozen assets and at least $300 billion of development financing. Those were proposed terms, not completed sales or disbursements.

Physical recovery would take longer. QatarEnergy expected LNG output to return to about 50% of capacity one month after safe passage through Hormuz resumed. That timetable matters even if the agreement is signed as expected on June 19: reopening a route and restoring production are separate steps, and the US fixed-income holiday will leave the next open session to absorb accumulated news.

Equities reversed part of Monday's advance. The S&P 500 fell 0.57%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 1.89% and the semiconductor index dropped 5.71%, with losses concentrated in technology after large prior gains. VIX rose 1.30% to 16.41, still 17.4% below a week earlier. The dollar index eased 0.09% to 99.54, and gold was nearly unchanged, up 0.07% to $4,330.90. These moves provided less uniform support for risk-taking than Monday's rally, even as cheaper energy helped Treasuries.

The immediate focus is June 17 retail sales at 08:30 ET, followed by the FOMC decision at 14:00 and Warsh's press conference at 14:30. A hold at 3.50%-3.75% is expected. Control-group spending, the projections and any tightening bias will help determine how far the front end follows the decline in energy-related inflation compensation.

Overseas, UK consumer prices arrive June 17 before the Bank of England's June 18 decision, with its policy rate at 3.75%. The Riksbank, Swiss National Bank and Norges Bank also decide over those two days, while Bank Indonesia and the Philippine central bank face currency and imported-inflation pressures. Vote splits and guidance will show how much room lower oil has created for patience.

June 18 brings $70 billion of 4-week and $75 billion of 8-week bill auctions at 11:30 ET, followed at 13:00 by a $24 billion reopening of the 1.250% 5-year TIPS. The 6-week bills sold Tuesday also settle that day. TIPS demand after the Fed decision and funding conditions around the settlements are worth watching before the full June 19 market closure.

overall_summary.headline: Long Treasuries gain as Brent falls below $80 and the 20-year sale draws buyers
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The long end joined the Treasury rally after lagging on Monday. Ten- and 30-year yields fell 4 basis points to 4.43% and 4.93%, while the 2-year declined 2 to 4.05%. Brent dropped 5.06% to $78.96; the 10-year breakeven fell 3 basis points to 2.29%, accounting for most of the nominal yield decline. The $13 billion 20-year reopening drew 2.75 times coverage, leaving dealers just 8.48%.

The Fed faces conflicting data before Warsh's first decision. Import prices rose 1.9% in May against a 1.0% forecast, including a 0.8% nonfuel increase. Housing starts fell 15.4% to a 1.18 million annualized pace, driven largely by volatile multifamily construction. Markets expect a 3.50%-3.75% hold but still assign roughly 75% odds to a hike before year-end.

Japan raised rates to 1% and long JGB yields rose, while Australia paused at 4.35% without ruling out another increase. Credit remained selective: STMicroelectronics marketed low-coupon convertibles, Nvidia's new bonds traded actively near issue prices, and Optimum and Brightline faced difficult liability negotiations. The Philippines completed its 2026 external commercial borrowing plan with an upsized $2.5 billion sale, even as technology shares fell sharply.
overall_summary.summary: Ten- and 30-year yields fell 4 basis points as lower inflation compensation and a strong 20-year auction supported duration. Hot import prices kept Fed hike risk alive despite a sharp decline in housing starts.

watch_events.watch_line: UK CPI precedes the BOE decision, with rates at 3.75%. Sweden, Switzerland, Norway, Indonesia and the Philippines also face policy decisions.
